prompt:
Use case: product-mockup. Create an industrial design concept image for a first FDM 3D printed automotive glovebox electronics enclosure. This is an appearance study, not validated CAD. Approximate external proportions 190mm wide x150mm deep x65mm tall: a substantial low rectangular box, not a tiny dongle. Contains Raspberry Pi 4, cellular modem, SSD, reserved power module. Small square 1.3-inch LCD with 23mm square visible active screen and exactly two small physical pushbuttons. Passive cooling slots, no fan. Internal antennas, no protruding antenna rods. Two-piece shell with real lid seam, visible recessed screw heads, replaceable small display bezel and rear cable panel. Single black USB cable exits through jacket strain relief. Manufacturable flat-bottom parts with modest corner radii and chamfers, no elaborate overhangs. Honest matte ASA plastic with subtle visible 0.2mm print layers, no shiny injection molded illusion. Photorealistic studio concept render on light neutral background, softly lit with detailed material texture. Landscape sheet with one large front/top three-quarter assembled view and one smaller rear three-quarter view of the SAME consistent design. Only text should be a discreet heading supplied below; screen has simple green status icon, no invented branding. Do not draw dimension arrows, certification marks, Tesla logos, phones, extra parts or implausible mechanisms.
Heading: '01 / MINIMAL'. Quiet restrained rounded rectangular shell in warm light gray ASA with dark charcoal removable display bezel on the top near the front, two small buttons alongside it. Small parallel ventilation slots towards rear of top, subtle lower side air inlets. Four lid screws. Smooth broad surfaces with soft 6mm corner radii, a clean horizontal seam near the top. A practical, unobtrusive appliance with thoughtful screw access.
